jobs.occupation: 1352 Postdoctoral position in marine ecological modelling
jobs.description:
About the Position
The Institute of Marine Research (IMR) offers a 3-year postdoctoral position as part of the MORSE (“Models supporting practical restoration of habitats and species in Europe’s seas”) research project funded by Horizon Europe. This project sits within IMR’s strategic initiative to build a strong center for marine research within one of Europe's largest marine research institutes. The candidate will ideally start in early 2027. 

We seek a postdoctoral researcher with a background in ecological modelling, with relevant experience and publication record on modelling marine and/or aquatic ecosystems. The postdoctoral researcher will work across several work packages, including WP5 (reviewing and compiling data on restoration pathways, pressures, and ecological needs of focal species and habitats, and defining favourable reference areas), WP6 (species distribution modelling and assessment of environmental status (NEAT), WP7 (modelling land-, and sea-based pressures, and MPAs), and WP8 (modelling ecosystem services). The broader aim of the project is to develop and demonstrate effective and climate-resilient restoration models for European marine ecosystems to inform more effective restoration efforts. 

The postdoctoral researcher will work with a team of researchers at IMR and collaborating partners to carry out and deliver research outcomes in the MORSE project. The MORSE project that the postdoctoral position is associated with is a 4-year project that is led by the Finnish Environmental Institute (SYKE) and includes institutions across seven European countries (Finland, Sweden, Norway, UK, Spain, Portugal, and Greece). Travel to workshops and meetings in these countries should be anticipated. The postdoctoral researcher will gain mentoring support, training, and networking opportunities from the leading researchers associated with the MORSE project, and have the opportunity to establish connections and advance their research career over the course of the project. More information about MORSE can be found at the project website: https://morse-project.eu/ 

Knowledge about northern European marine ecosystems is an advantage, as the postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for modelling Norwegian marine ecosystems. The position is placed within the Benthic Communities research group and can be located at any of the IMR offices. Note that the IMR project lead (Karine Gagnon) is based at Flødevigen Research Station, but the research group includes members across all three locations. IMR has good links and cooperation with industry, management, and the university sector. We offer the opportunity to be part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary, and ambitious research group with strong national and international links.

Main tasks:

• Lead and support MORSE research activities as directed by project leaders. 
• Write research publications, reports, and grant proposals.
• Participate in scientific conferences, science communication, and outreach activities. 
• Review and compile existing data on restoration pathways, ecosystem status, and pressures for focal species and habitats, and define favourable reference areas for these 
• Review and compile existing models and data sources for the Norwegian sea areas (including the Skagerrak, Norwegian Sea, North Sea, and Barents Sea) 
• Apply species distribution models and assess environmental status using the NEAT tool 
• Model land-based and sea-based pressures on marine habitats, and the role of MPAs 
• Model climate scenarios and ecosystem services 
• Participate in work package coordination and reporting 
• Maintain and curate datasets and coordinate data sharing and modelling efforts across MORSE partners.About the Research Group and Our Work
The Benthic Communities group focuses on research, mapping, and monitoring of benthic ecosystems, including seagrass meadows, macroalgae forests, and deep-sea ecosystems. Research within the project will support IMR’s national advisory task on ecosystem-based management of seas and coastal areas, where environmental changes and human activities and are important factors. The research group has over 30 employees base on Flødevigen, Bergen, and Tromsø.
Qualification Requirements
For this position, we are looking for a candidate with

• PhD in biology or ecology, preferably with a focus on ecological modelling
• Documented experience in ecological modelling 
• Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral skills in English
The working language at the Institute of Marine Research is Norwegian. Being able to communicate well in Norwegian is an important prerequisite for both the employee and our institute. We expect non-Norwegian-speaking employees to complete Norwegian language courses during the first two years of employment. The institute will cover the cost of completed and passed Norwegian courses.
Personal Qualities
At the Institute of Marine Research, we believe that personality plays a role in how one works, communicates, and thrives in the workplace. For this position, we are looking for a colleague who

• Good communication and collaboration skills. 
• Good organisational and logistics skills. 
• Ability to complete work on time and meeting deadline 
• Ability to work efficiently independently and in teams.Desired Qualifications
• Strong skills and experience in ecological modelling and data analysis
• Ability and willingness to collaborate with colleagues in Norway and abroad 
• Ability and willingness to organize and lead joint modelling efforts with partners abroad 
• Research experience in marine ecosystems, species, and habitats 
• Research experience in ecological restoration and/or conservationInclusion and Diversity is a Strength
The Institute of Marine Research believes that inclusion and diversity are strengths. Therefore, we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for a position with us, regardless of age, gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic background. The Institute is an Inclusive Workplace (IA) company, and we aim to accommodate applicants with disabilities.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, employment gaps, or immigrant backgrounds, we will invite at least one applicant from each of these groups to an interview. To be considered for affirmative action, you must meet the requirements and indicate that you wish to be considered for the action in your application. You can read more here.
Your application must include 
• a cover letter describing your research interests and motivation for applying for the position. The letter should not exceed one A4 page.• Full name and contact details for two or three referees, preferably your PhD supervisor and/or references from recent employment.• CV, transcripts, diplomas, and relevant certificates.• A list of scientific publications, if applicable.

All documents must be in a Scandinavian language or in English. Candidates with documentation from foreign institutions must include an explanation of the institution’s grading system.
We offer
• the opportunity to work in one of Europe’s leading marine research institutes
• a creative working environment
• facilities in either Flødevigen, Bergen or Tromsø 
• flexible work hours 
• public sector occupational pension through the Norwegian Public Service Pension Funds (SPK)
• access to company cabins, fitness facilities, and other welfare benefitsAditional information
The position is remunerated as 1352 Postdoctoral in accordance with the main collective agreement in the state sector, depending on your qualifications and the characteristics of the position. A 2 % contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge.

Please note that information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has requested not to be listed. Applicants will be informed in advance if such disclosure is necessary.

The Institute of Marine Research is subject to export control regulations. These regulations apply to the processing of applications for the position.

Applicants with education from abroad may be asked to provide NOKUT approval of their qualifications. You may be asked to approve that the Institute of Marine Research conducts a background check.

jobs.occupation: PhD position in Aluminium Extrusion
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) has a vacancy for a PhD candidate within aluminium extrusion, associated with the Centre for Research-based Innovation SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures.

The position is a  3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in 2026. The PhD candidate will be embedded in the forming research activities of SFI FAST  and will work closely with NTNU, SINTEF, and leading international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain (Hydro, Benteler Automotive, Raufoss Technology, Speira, Raufoss Aluminium, Renault, etc).

This PhD position focuses on aluminium extrusion of profiles based on high recycled content. The research will address process–microstructure–property relationships, weld integrity, die design, and product quality in extrusion of complex profiles from post-consumer scrap aluminium (PCS).

The use of PCS in the production of structural components (i.e. automotive) is currently limited but is expected to grow as more stringent sustainability requirements and regulations come into effect. The candidate will establish and validate numerical forming simulations, predict PCS effects on seam- and charge weld quality, surface quality, integrate microstructure and texture evolution into the models, integrate quenching sequence in modelling, conduct industrial experiments, and demonstrate validity through use-cases in the project. The foci of the research work include practical experiments (including extrusion experiments, and mechanical/microstructure characterization tests), theoretical analysis, and numerical simulation. 

The candidate will work in collaboration with industrial partners and needs to be responsible for reporting progress and delivering outputs to the FAST centre. S/he will have the possibility to obtain a cotutelle (‘dual’) PhD degree between NTNU and University of Bologna, Italy.
About SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures
SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminum industry. The centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 16 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. FAST runs from 2026 to 2033 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy.

The primary objective of FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance.

A key outcome of FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains.

Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. The two positions posted here will be among the first ones to start in the center. 
Duties of the position
• Study, prototype and validate extrusion processes mechanisms for improved accuracy and mechanical properties
• Investigate the impact of thermal-mechanical processing on the subsequent forming processes and end-product quality
• Perform mechanical and microstructural testing, characterization and analysis to assess the properties of material and components
• Investigate the process behaviours, mechanisms and models to improve and optimize the process capabilities
• Conduct and publish high-level research at peer-reviewed journals and international conferences
• Work closely with industry and employ the industry-as-laboratory concept for extrusion trials and studies
• Participate and contribute to research group and FAST WP3 (Forming) activities, including mentoring and supervising MScs
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Materials Science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Strong academic background relevant to metal forming or aluminium processing
• You must have experience in continuum-based modelling using FEA software
• Good written and oral English skills
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge and testing skills in material characterization and microstructural analysis of aluminium alloys, using advance equipment like SEM, TEM, P-FIB, etc.
• Experience in the design and development of machine tools in metal forming processes
• Experience in using alternative, relevant modelling methods for material, process, and product behaviour (like using analytical, data-driven modelling approaches, AI, etc.)
• Background from or knowing the NTNU/Norwegian  or University of Bologna university system to be prepared for following the mandatory exchange path associated with a cotutelle PhD degree
• Experience with industrial research and industry-as-a-laboratory type of activitiesPersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Highly motivated
• Able to work independently
• Curious and enthusiastic
• Strong ability to systematically carry out goal-oriented work
• Enjoy and contribute to interdisciplinary research
• Keen interest in learning and working in teams
• Good skills to deliver oral and written presentation of research results
• Strong interest in combining theory and practice through experimental and numerical research
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer

• SFI FAST facilities, industrial network, and a joint PhD environment

• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment

• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)

As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a PhD Research Fellow position in Mathematics, available at the Department of Mathematics, as part of QSTAR – Centre for quantum computing and applications.

Starting date as soon as possible and no later than 01.04.2027.

The fellowship period is three years.

A fourth year may be considered, and it will involve 25 % of other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This is dependent upon the qualifications of the applicant and the current needs of the department.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo.

Place of work is Department of Mathematics/QSTAR at Blindern, Oslo.
Job description
The position is affiliated with QSTAR - Centre for Quantum Computing and Applications. QSTAR is a five-year research centre funded by the Research Council of Norway (project number 361617) and hosted and led by SINTEF. It brings together researchers at SINTEF, UiO, NTNU, OsloMet and Simula Research Laboratory, with international partners at the University of Copenhagen and RISE in Sweden.

The centre connects four research work packages: fault tolerance and error correction; compilation and Hamiltonian engineering; foundations of quantum algorithms; and quantum algorithms for applications. Together, they address how quantum information can be protected, how algorithms can be implemented, and where quantum computation may offer advantages, particularly in chemistry and optimisation.

PhD candidates become part of a research community spanning mathematics, physics, chemistry and optimisation. The centre’s programme includes seminars, PhD schools, annual retreats and conferences, alongside opportunities for international exchange and collaboration across partner institutions.

ARENA Centre for European Studies at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) in political science or another relevant social science discipline. The position is for a period of three years, with no teaching or other required duties. 

The place of work is ARENA Centre for European Studies, University of Oslo.
 
ARENA is an interdisciplinary research centre at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. Since 1994, the centre has studied political, security, economic, legal and social integration, transformation and cooperation in Europe. ARENA has extensive experience in coordinating international research projects and networks funded by European and Norwegian institutions. 

The centre has around 30 academic and four administrative staff. More information about ARENA is available here.
More about the position 
Europe is being reshaped by war, geopolitical rivalry and a renewed enlargement agenda. As the EU's rules and decisions reach further beyond its borders, Norway faces key questions about alignment, influence and democratic control. Norway is one of the most closely integrated non-member states. That makes it an important case for understanding what it means to be part of European integration without being a member of the Union.

ARENA is looking for a PhD Research Fellow who wants to write a dissertation on Norway's relationship with the EU. The successful candidate will develop and carry out their own doctoral project in a research environment with long experience of studying European integration and its consequences for countries both inside and outside the Union.

We expect theoretically informed empirical studies and particularly welcome projects that take a comparative approach, but single-case studies of Norway are also welcome. Examples of comparisons could include comparing and contrasting Norway with other associated or third countries (such as Iceland, Switzerland or the United Kingdom), EU member states or candidate countries. Comparisons across policy areas are also welcome. We are open to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches.

Relevant research areas could include, but are not limited to:

• Norway's association model: Projects could for example address how the EEA Agreement and Norway's many other agreements with the EU shape Norwegian politics, public administration and regulation, or how they compare with those of comparable EU member or affiliated states. Projects could look at Norway's room for manoeuvre and influence vis-à-vis the EU, at questions of democratic legitimacy and control, or at how the association model is evolving as the EU changes. 
• Justice and home affairs: Projects could for example address Norway's participation in Schengen, European migration and asylum policy, border management, or police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. Projects could study how EU developments in these fields affect Norwegian policies, institutions and societal security, possibly compared with other associated or member countries.
We are looking for candidates with interesting and relevant research ideas, strong theoretical and analytical skills, and solid methodological competence. The project proposal should combine clear theoretical and empirical ambitions with a realistic and feasible research design.

Electrochemistry is a truly interdisciplinary field drawing on chemistry, physics, materials science, electronics, and nanotechnology alike. Electrochemistry therefore offers unique possibilities for interesting scientific work and an exciting career. Electrochemistry is essential in current pursuit of the green transition and the establishing of a sustainable society, as it is critical to some pivotal technologies such as hydrogen technology (water electrolysis and fuel cells), and batteries. It is also critical to the manufacture of materials that go into a diverse set of technologies related to energy storage and renewables. The demand for staff with expertise in Electrochemistry is therefore soaring.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The available PhD position is affiliated with the research HYDROGENi centre for hydrogen technology (https://hydrogeni.no/), one of several Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research funded by the Norwegian Research Council and major energy and industry companies. The HYDROGENi centre constitutes a strong team of research and industry partners and globally leading universities and research centres. The PhD student will participate in a network of PhD students and industrialists across disciplines and will participate in summer and winter schools organised by the centre in addition to the training offered by the PhD programme itself. The primary objective of the PhD work will be to establish analysis tools for performance and degradation of electrocatalyst layers for alkaline electrolyte membrane water electrolysis.

The PhD student will have access to state-of-the-art equipment for manufacture and in situ characterization of performance and degradation processes in electrocatalyst layers.

• Experimental electrochemistry and characterization of degradation processes (voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, chronoamperometry and others, including in-situ and in-line methods)

The Norwegian Defence Command and Staff College (Stabsskolen), part of the Norwegian Defence University College (NDUC/FHS), is seeking an experienced researcher to strengthen its activities in wargaming. This role offers a unique opportunity to establish and shape a long-term academic environment for wargaming at NDUC, while working closely with researchers, military practitioners, NATO partners, and other stakeholders and partners.

NDUC has campuses in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim, and Lillehammer.
